title: Queen and pawn forks
line: The queen attacks in eight directions; the pawn, the smallest piece, attacks two bigger ones.

steps.text: The queen looks in eight directions at once. A queen check that also hits a loose piece is a fork.
Fork the king and the rook with one queen move.
steps.hint: Find a square on the diagonal to the king and on the diagonal to the rook.
steps.after: Check, and the rook in the corner is attacked too.

steps.text: The king had to step aside. Take the rook.
A pawn can fork too. It attacks two squares diagonally forward, and it is worth less than anything it attacks.
Tap the square where a white pawn would attack the knight and the bishop at once.
steps.hint: The pawn has to land between the two black pieces, one rank below them.
steps.after: From there the pawn attacks both pieces.
One piece can step away, but not both. And the other white pawn guards the forking one.

steps.text: The knight ran. Take the bishop.
steps.after: The pawn on f7 takes back: a bishop for a pawn.

summary: The queen forks with a check and a loose piece. A pawn forks two pieces that are each worth more than it.
